Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Austin/San Antonio TX
527 AM CST Sun Feb 15 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Elevated to near critical fire weather conditions for the southern 
  Edwards Plateau and Rio Grande Plains Sunday.

- Above normal temperatures and dry weather continues through the
  week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Monday)
Issued at 1206 AM CST Sun Feb 15 2026

Drier air is now spreading across South-Central Texas as Saturday's 
rainmaker leaves the area. Surface high pressure will gradually move 
over the area today, helping to bring a breezy north wind throughout 
the morning and early afternoon before the pressure gradient 
relaxes. Sustained winds are expected to top out at 15-20 mph for 
most of the area with gusts to 25-30 mph in the late morning before 
subsiding in the afternoon. Highs today range from near 70 north of 
I-10 to the low 80s in the Rio Grande Plains under mostly clear 
skies. 

Deep layer ridging will become better established over our area 
Monday, bringing much more seasonably cool temperatures early Monday 
morning with lows in the 40s to low 50s. Those conditions won't last 
for long. A southerly to southwesterly flow should quickly return in 
response to pressure falls over the Northern Plains. Highs Monday 
will be back in the upper 70s to mid 80s. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Monday night through Saturday)
Issued at 1206 AM CST Sun Feb 15 2026

Over the course of the week, the upper level ridge of our area 
should gradually move east and flatten out. While this allows west-
southwesterly flow in the upper-levels, moisture will be largely 
absent from this flow so dry weather will prevail. Underneath, 
southwesterly flow in the mid- to low-levels will repeatedly cycle 
warm Mexican plateau air over South-Central Texas, leading to an 
unseasonably warm midweek period with highs in the mid-80s to low-
90s. These values are about 15 to 20 degrees above the average for 
late February. Overnight lows are forecast to be in the mid 50s to 
low 60s midweek. 

One or more dry fronts will move through or make a glancing pass of 
South-Central Texas during the week as several shortwave troughs 
rotate about broader troughing across the Intermountain West. The 
first front on Wednesday lacks much northerly flow aloft behind it, 
so its impact on our weather should be minimal. A second front later 
in the week on Friday has been advertised on ensembles for some time 
and may moderate temperatures slightly with the aid of brief 
northwesterly flow at 850mb. This shaves off a few degrees in the 
forecast for next weekend with highs lower but still remaining above-
average in the 70s. The ensemble guidance and ML-driven global 
models hint at a low chance for light rain next weekend associated 
with that second front, but confidence is too low to highlight this 
in the gridded forecast. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 527 AM CST Sun Feb 15 2026

VFR flying conditions prevail today through Monday most areas, 
except SCT-BKN MVFR clouds over Central Texas/KAUS this morning 
into early afternoon. There are moderate to high probabilities for
VLIFR/LIFR CIGs/VSBYs at the I-35 sites early to mid Monday 
morning. Northerly winds increase to 10 to 19 KTs with gusts to 28
KTs by mid morning, decrease late this afternoon, and then become
light tonight.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1206 AM CST Sun Feb 15 2026

Breezy conditions are forecast Sunday morning through the afternoon 
as dry northwesterly winds develop in the wake of yesterday's storm 
system. Minimum relative humidity values west of I-10 (north of San 
Antonio)/I-37 will drop below 30 percent with sustained 20 ft winds 
of 10-15 mph along the Rio Grande and along Hill Country ridgelines, 
supporting elevated to near critical fire weather conditions. Winds 
weaken Sunday evening and southerly flow returns Monday. Drier air 
and unseasonably warm conditions will remain in place for much of 
the week, so additional elevated fire weather days are possible.
